briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for November 3, 2026. Today, various efforts to raise awareness of the climate crisis and achieve carbon neutrality have been reported both domestically and internationally, and global calls for climate action are continuing ahead of the upcoming COP31.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Rising Climate Crisis Awareness and Public Participation
sections.content: Recently, awareness of the climate crisis has been very high domestically, with 94% of Koreans supporting methane reduction and climate change concern ranking first among 18 countries [1]. Such concerns also lead to questions about the impact on daily life, such as 'changes in beer taste' [3]. In response, Daegu City is actively encouraging citizen participation through campaigns like 'Save Daefrica,' which promotes carbon neutrality practices and offers events such as gift certificates worth up to 100,000 KRW [12, 13, 14, 17, 19, 26, 31, 36, 37]. Furthermore, policies encouraging daily life practices are expanding, including the inclusion of 'reusable delivery boxes' in the Carbon Neutrality Point System [15] and Gyeongsan City's support for enrollment [16, 34]. The Incheon Institute suggested that the effects of carbon neutrality should consider not only greenhouse gas reduction but also citizen health [18, 24], emphasizing the importance of climate action. Guro-gu's 'Climate Action Essay Contest' [20] and Gwangmyeong City's designation as a citizen-led environmental education city [28, 39] are contributing to the spread of a public participation-oriented climate response culture.

sections.title: 🌱 Efforts and Challenges for Achieving Carbon Neutrality Goals
sections.content: Domestically, multifaceted efforts to achieve carbon neutrality goals are continuing. The Seoul Institute has agreed to jointly respond to climate change and AI issues with research institutions from major global cities [2], and Samsung Electronics and Doosan Enerbility have received positive evaluations in ESG branding for their carbon neutrality and energy-saving efforts [7]. Amid claims that the cost of implementing carbon neutrality is less than the cost of neglecting the climate crisis [8], various local governments and organizations, including Dangjin City [9], Seodaemun-gu [11], and Oga-myeon Saemaul Association in Yesan-gun [22, 41], are spreading carbon neutrality practices through events such as the 'Carbon Neutrality Family Golden Bell,' energy foundation agreements, and upcycling education. Meanwhile, 41 global organizations urged the expansion of nuclear power generation at COP31, pointing out the limitations of achieving carbon neutrality without nuclear power [6], and new challenges are emerging, such as concerns that the surge in data centers in the U.S. could negate greenhouse gas reduction efforts due to AI [10]. Gangwon Province's achievement rate for greenhouse gas reduction targets was the third lowest nationwide [30], suggesting the need for efforts to reduce regional disparities.

sections.title: ⚠️ Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Policy Recommendations
sections.content: Ahead of the 100GW era of renewable energy, there is a growing call for urgent innovation in power grid operation, electricity markets, and regulatory frameworks [42, 47, 52, 57, 62, 65]. The RE100 initiative strongly urged the Korean government to broaden avenues for corporate renewable energy procurement and to include renewable energy expansion and corporate procurement measures in the 12th Basic Plan for Long-term Electricity Supply and Demand (Electricity Basic Plan) [46, 50, 53, 59]. As a positive sign, Busan Port is pursuing an 'energy self-sufficient port' that directly produces and consumes renewable energy [43], and five power generation companies have merged after 25 years, anticipating expanded renewable energy and improved management efficiency [44]. Furthermore, overseas investment and technological cooperation are active, with Woori Bank executing large-scale loans for new and renewable energy projects in India [45] and TotalEnergies expanding its wind power investments in the U.S. [58, 51]. However, areas requiring policy improvement have also become clear, such as electricity tariffs and grid usage fees acting as obstacles to renewable energy expansion in the Jeju region [60], and cases where renewable energy investments are excluded from greenhouse gas reduction management targets [61]. The argument that renewable energy transition must align with economic and industrial strategies [48] also presents an important policy direction.

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Crisis Warnings and COP31 Discussions
sections.content: Ahead of the upcoming COP31 Climate Change Summit, warnings and discussions about the climate crisis are active within the international community [72, 80, 82, 83, 84, 89, 101, 105]. UN reports are highlighting the severity by warning of large-scale damage to the Earth's ice due to climate change [81, 94]. The impacts of climate change are manifesting as concrete damages, including not only rising temperatures in tropical regions [69] but also 8,830 additional premature births during India's April 2024 heatwave [100] and a $17.5 billion income loss in Bangladesh [79]. Furthermore, research findings have been published indicating that anxiety about climate change can cause mental health difficulties for students [73, 77, 95], raising the need for a human security-oriented response. Criticism of Canada for positioning itself as a climate leader at COP31 despite policy setbacks [90, 97, 99], and a report that the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) does not consider climate change a 'major' financial risk [92], demonstrate a skeptical view of the international community's climate policy implementation. Amidst this, efforts to establish a scientific basis continue, with IPCC authors discussing progress on the physical science report on climate change in Tanzania [102].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing clearly demonstrated the growing awareness of the climate crisis, the diverse domestic and international efforts to address it, and the complex challenges simultaneously faced. In particular, the acceleration of renewable energy transition and the international community's strong call for climate action will be addressed as even more critical agenda items at the upcoming COP31. This concludes today's climate briefing.
